hook.line: In a meeting somebody says you promised something. You are not sure, and you don't want to call anyone a liar. This is the polite way to say it did not happen as far as you recall.
hook.es: No recuerdo que dijera eso exactamente.
hook.en: I don't recall him saying exactly that.

examples.es: No recuerdo que dijera eso exactamente.
examples.en: I don't recall him saying exactly that.

examples.es: No me acuerdo de que me lo prometieras.
examples.en: I don't remember you promising it to me.

examples.es: No recuerdo que Vale llamara esa noche.
examples.en: I don't recall Vale calling that night.

examples.es: No recuerdo que hablaran del precio.
examples.en: I don't recall them talking about the price.
I remember that he said that.

examples.en: I don't remember where I left the keys.

rule:
When you remember something, use the indicative: *recuerdo que dijo eso*.

When you don't, the verb after *que* switches to the past subjunctive: *no recuerdo que dijera eso*. It says: I'm not vouching that this happened. It sounds polite and firm.

English says "I don't remember him saying". Spanish uses *que* and a full verb: *dijera*, *llamara*, *hablaran*, *prometieras*.

With *acordarse* add *de*: *no me acuerdo de que…*

A question word is different: *no me acuerdo de dónde dejé las llaves*, plain indicative.
smallPrint: Teachers call *dijera* the imperfect subjunctive. Here it works as a polite way to not confirm what someone else claims.

readAndPick.es: No recuerdo que dijera eso exactamente.
options: I recall him saying exactly that.
I don't recall him saying exactly that.
I don't recall you saying exactly that.
I don't remember that he said that.
I wonder whether he said that.
I remember that he said that.

readAndPick.es: No me acuerdo de que me lo prometieras.
options: I don't remember you promising it to me.
I don't remember them promising it to me.
I don't remember promising it to you.

readAndPick.es: No recuerdo que hablaran del precio.
options: I don't recall us talking about the price.
I don't recall you talking about the price.
I don't recall them talking about the price.

readAndPick.es: No recuerdo que Vale llamara esa noche.
options: I recall Vale calling that night.
I don't recall Vale calling that night.
I don't recall calling Vale that night.

readAndPick.es: No me acuerdo de dónde dejé las llaves.
options: I don't remember where I left the keys.
I don't remember where you left the keys.
I don't remember where I'm leaving the keys.

readAndPick.es: Me acuerdo de que llegaste tarde.
options: I don't remember that you arrived late.
I remember that I arrived late.
I remember that you arrived late.

readAndPick.es: No recuerdo que nadie votara en contra.
options: I recall nobody voting against.
I don't recall anyone voting against.
I don't recall anyone voting in favour.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *dijo* or *dijera*: No recuerdo que ___ eso exactamente. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: No recuerdo que dijera eso exactamente.
yourTurn.why: When you don't remember it, the verb after *que* is in the subjunctive: *dijera*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *llegaste* or *llegaras*: Me acuerdo de que ___ tarde. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Me acuerdo de que llegaste tarde.
yourTurn.why: Remembering it means it happened, so the indicative: *llegaste*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I don't recall Vale calling that night.
yourTurn.answer: No recuerdo que Vale llamara esa noche.
accept: No me acuerdo de que Vale llamara esa noche.
yourTurn.why: The verb after *que* is *llamara*, the subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I don't remember you promising it to me.
yourTurn.answer: No me acuerdo de que me lo prometieras.
accept: No recuerdo que me lo prometieras.
yourTurn.why: *Prometieras* ends in *-ras* because it is about *you*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I don't remember where I left the keys.
yourTurn.answer: No me acuerdo de dónde dejé las llaves.
accept: No recuerdo dónde dejé las llaves.
yourTurn.why: After a question word, the verb stays in the plain indicative: *dejé*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn *Recuerdo que dijo eso.* into a doubt: say you don't remember it.
accept: No me acuerdo de que dijera eso.
yourTurn.why: Not remembering moves the verb to the subjunctive: *dijera*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I don't recall anyone voting against.
yourTurn.answer: No recuerdo que nadie votara en contra.
accept: No me acuerdo de que nadie votara en contra.
yourTurn.why: *Votara* is the subjunctive for one person, here *nadie*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. When you are not vouching for it, the verb after *que* takes the subjunctive.

pitfalls.wrong: No me acuerdo que me lo prometieras.
pitfalls.right: No me acuerdo de que me lo prometieras.

pitfalls.wrong: No recuerdo a Vale llamando esa noche.
pitfalls.right: No recuerdo que Vale llamara esa noche.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "Vale calling", but Spanish uses *que* and a full verb.

personal: Imagine a friend says you promised to do something. Answer politely, starting with *No recuerdo que…* or *No me acuerdo de que…*.
